attachments.insertion_landmark: coronoid process of mandible (via a fan-shaped tendon)

actions: posterior fibers retract a protruded mandible

functional_compartments.name: Anterior part (near-vertical fibers)
functional_compartments.function_note: Near-vertical fiber orientation gives the anterior part the largest elevating moment arm; the primary contributor to bite force.
functional_compartments.source: van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

functional_compartments.name: Posterior part (near-horizontal fibers)
functional_compartments.function_note: Near-horizontal fiber orientation over the posterior temporal fossa gives this part a retractive (posteriorly-directed) moment arm, mainly recruited to retract a protruded mandible rather than to elevate it -- a real fiber-direction-driven functional split within one named muscle.
functional_compartments.source: van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region
